holidays.name: National Simplicity Day
holidays.description: A day to declutter your schedule, clear off your desk and remember that less really can be more. Spend the day unplugging, skipping the to-do list and enjoying the small things.
holidays.origin: The day falls on the birthday of writer and philosopher Henry David Thoreau, born July 12, 1817. He is famous for living simply at Walden Pond and writing about it.
holidays.funFact: Thoreau lived in his small cabin at Walden Pond for two years, two months and two days. He built it himself for about $28.

holidays.name: Different Colored Eyes Day
holidays.description: A celebration of people whose eyes are two different colors, or have two tones within one eye. It's a day to appreciate one of nature's rarest quirks.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on quirky holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: The condition is called heterochromia, and it affects well under 1% of people. Celebrities such as Kate Bosworth and Mila Kunis are known for it.

holidays.name: National Pecan Pie Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in the gooey, nutty, sugary classic of Southern kitchens. Bake one, buy one, or top a slice with vanilla ice cream.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It gives dessert lovers a reason to enjoy pecan pie in the middle of summer, not just at Thanksgiving.
holidays.funFact: The pecan is the only major tree nut native to North America. Its name comes from an Algonquian word for nuts that need a stone to crack.
